# sonarqube_gitlab_configuration (Resource)

GitLab authentication and provisioning. SonarQube has one such configuration; destroying the resource deletes it. It is stored in the `sonar.auth.gitlab.*` settings, which must not also be managed with `sonarqube_setting`. Import ID: the configuration ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Log in with a self-managed GitLab, adding users at their first login to the
# SonarQube groups named like their GitLab groups.
resource "sonarqube_gitlab_configuration" "main" {
  enabled                = true
  url                    = "https://gitlab.example.com"
  application_id         = "0123456789abcdef"
  secret_wo              = var.gitlab_secret
  credentials_wo_version = "1"
  allowed_groups         = ["engineering"]
  provisioning_type      = "JIT"
  synchronize_groups     = true
}

variable "gitlab_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `application_id` (String) Application ID of the GitLab application.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether users can log in with GitLab.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `allow_all_groups` (Boolean) With `AUTO_PROVISIONING`, provision every group the provisioning token can see and ignore `allowed_groups`. Not allowed with gitlab.com.
- `allow_users_to_sign_up` (Boolean) With `JIT`, whether users who do not exist in SonarQube yet can sign up. Defaults to the server's choice.
- `allowed_groups` (Set of String) Root groups whose members (subgroups included) can log in, and are provisioned with `AUTO_PROVISIONING`. `AUTO_PROVISIONING` needs at least one, unless `allow_all_groups` is set.
- `credentials_wo_version` (String) Any value; changing it applies the current values of the `_wo` arguments.
- `provisioning_token` (String, Sensitive) GitLab token with `read_api` scope, needed by `AUTO_PROVISIONING`. Stored in state; prefer `provisioning_token_wo`. SonarQube does not return it, so drift cannot be detected.
- `provisioning_token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only form of `provisioning_token`, never stored in state (Terraform 1.11+). Change `credentials_wo_version` to apply a new value.
- `provisioning_type` (String) `JIT` creates users at their first login. `AUTO_PROVISIONING` synchronizes the members of the allowed groups with SonarQube hourly; it needs Developer edition or above.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Secret of the GitLab application. Stored in state; prefer `secret_wo`. SonarQube does not return it, so drift cannot be detected.
- `secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only form of `secret`, never stored in state (Terraform 1.11+). Change `credentials_wo_version` to apply a new value.
- `synchronize_groups` (Boolean) With `JIT`, add users at login to the SonarQube groups named like their GitLab groups or teams.
- `url` (String) URL of the GitLab instance.

### Read-Only

- `error_message` (String) Why SonarQube considers the configuration invalid, if it does.
- `id` (String) Configuration ID.
- `provisioning_token_set` (Boolean) Whether SonarQube has a provisioning token.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sonarqube_gitlab_configuration.example 'gitlab-configuration'
```
